glosses: mit Genuss essen; etwas Leckeres essen

examples.text: Nach der Wanderung schmausten wir unsere mitgebrachten Leckereien.

translations.source_sense_description: mit Genuss essen; etwas Leckeres essen

glosses: A holiday, festival, especially a religious one

examples.text: The seventh day shall be a feast to the Lord.
Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover.

glosses: A very large meal, often of a ceremonial nature.

examples.text: We had a feast to celebrate the harvest.
It was a feast for the eyes.

glosses: To partake in a feast, or large meal.

examples.text: I feasted on turkey and dumplings.
With my love's picture then my eye doth feast.

glosses: To hold a feast in honor of (someone).

examples.text:
He that shall see this day, and live old age,
Will yearly on the vigil feast his neighbors
And say “Tomorrow is Saint Crispian.”
His ancestor, he said, had been feasted there, when he went forward with the then Lord Ravenswood to the fatal battle of Flodden, in which they both fell.
We feasted them after the victory.

glosses: To serve as a feast for; to feed sumptuously.

examples.text:
1597–1598, Joseph Hall, Virgidemiarum
Or once a week, perhaps, for novelty / Reez'd bacon-soords shall feast his family.

translations.source_sense_description: mit Genuss essen; etwas Leckeres essen

glosses: Prendre beaucoup de plaisir à quelque chose, en particulier à un spectacle ou à l’audition, à la lecture d’un scandale.
vi. 大吃大喝，津津有味地吃
